note: Web bundle 11 - diagnostics for the scroll problem; no reading behaviour changes. Bundles 9 and 10 both left scrolling not working in Joshua's hands on the TCL while the same code scrolled in desktop Chrome, so this bundle stops guessing and measures the scroll path on the phone itself. About a second after a book opens it checks: which bundle is truly running versus which the shell is serving; whether the book's scroll container holds more stream than window, and by how much; whether setting that container's scroll position in code actually moves it; how each live section's frame compares with its content height; and, with passive watch-only listeners that cannot interfere with a drag, what one real finger drag delivers to the handlers and whether the container moves under it. Findings go home through the same Reader Report pipe as reader errors, the headline appears in a long toast at book open, and everything is kept for the shelf's new Diagnostics button, which shows the measurement and can send it on demand. Next to that evidence, the fix that follows will be aimed instead of blind. Reading behaviour is otherwise exactly bundle 10's.
